key_insight: A joint spatial–physical coupling operator explicitly models local interactions among flow variables to improve super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulence.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help reconstruct detailed turbulent flow fields from low-resolution data constrained by hardware and computational costs.
method: Extend standard convolution into a joint spatial–variable dimension.
Lift features into a higher-dimensional representation to capture local cross-variable interactions.
Integrate the architecture-agnostic operator into CNN-based super-resolution models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong reconstruction performance and zero-shot generalization in experiments, but provides no datasets, quantitative metrics, or evaluation details.
watch_item: The computational and memory costs of the higher-dimensional representation are not specified in the abstract.
paper_title: A high-dimensional spatial-physical coupling operator for generalizable super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulent flows
